subject: Re: Checkout slow tails & elevated error-rate — FastGate escalation and mitigation
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@fastgate.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Checkout transactions timing out / p99 spikes — urgent

Hi Rafael,

We started seeing sustained checkout failures and long tail latencies this morning across multiple regions. P95 is fine but p99s are climbing above 10s and a number of customers are reporting timeouts; error-rate has ticked up ~2.5% on POST /v1/generate-checkout. This is causing payment flows to bail and support tickets are spiking.

We rely on the Redwood hosted route for our recommendations and are seeing both long completion times and occasional 502s. Can you confirm whether this is related to the rollout from last night or capacity? We need an ETA on resolution — our CS and ops teams are asking for an executive contact.

Attached: brief CSV with affected request IDs (ids.csv stub).

— Samir
Ops Lead, FastGate Commerce
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastgate.com>, ops@fastgate.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-11T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout transactions timing out / p99 spikes — urgent

Samir — thanks for the heads-up and sorry for the customer impact. We're treating this as a high-priority escalation.

Quick notes / asks so we can triage faster:
- Can you confirm an approximate % of active checkouts affected and whether failures map to a particular region or model endpoint?
- If possible, please share two synthetic request IDs that reproduce a timeout (you provided a CSV; we'll use those).
- We're kicking the oncall infra/serving team now.

Initial hypothesis: early indicators point to a request pile-up in the routing layer combined with a concurrency cap we set in the dedicated pool — that combination can create long tails when backpressure propagates into upstream queues. We'll validate traces and KV-cache hit rates.

I'll loop in Hannah for exec visibility if this is an SLA risk. Meanwhile Marcus will run a quick trace aggregation and Marissa will look at routing/queueing telemetry. Expect a short update within 30–45 minutes.

— Rafael Mendes
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fast initial triage — traces and queueing

Rafael / Marissa,

Triage notes (10:05 PDT):
- Observed request queue depth increased on the us-west-2 router pool beginning 08:50 PDT. Queue growth correlates with a spike of large-checkout payloads (avg token window +200).
- Concurrency cap for FastGate's dedicated shard = 24 concurrent streams. At the time of the spike many streams were pinned due to long-running requests; admission control dropped a subset which surfaced as 502s.
- KV-cache miss rate increased ~4x for FastGate's model variant (likely because customers moved to longer contexts). Increased KV miss amplifies per-token work and elongates completions.
- We also saw intermittent backend worker GC pauses (~50–120ms) on two GPUs hosting FastGate; not dominant but contributed to tail.

Actions taken so far:
1) Temporarily bumped FastGate's concurrency cap to 40 on the us-west-2 dedicated shard (immediate relief in tail but capacity cost will increase).
2) Enabled prefix caching for stable checkout prompts for FastGate (should reduce KV misses for repeated templates).
3) Rolled a transient routing policy to prefer lower-utilization hosts for FastGate traffic.

Immediate result: p99 improved from ~12s → ~4.6s within 12 minutes; error-rate fell to 0.6%. Need to monitor for re-accumulation and cost impact.

I captured a trace snapshot and exported a CSV of affected request IDs (attached: trace_snapshot_20280511.txt).

— Marcus
Servicing & Reliability

Hannah — forwarding the thread + Marcus' initial triage. Summary: FastGate saw a sharp rise in long-context checkouts that exposed a concurrency cap + KV-miss amplification; we applied short-term mitigations (concurrency bump, prefix caching, routing tweak) with good immediate effect but cost will go up if sustained.

As this touches an enterprise account and SLA risk, request:
- Exec approval to keep elevated concurrency for the next 6 hours while we stabilize and run a targeted canary of the prefix-cache change.
- Authorization to offer FastGate a 10% usage credit for the incident window if we don't hit our SLOs in the next 24h.
- Ask SRE to run a focused pod-level GC and GPU health sweep on the two hosts I flagged.

Attaching: fastgate_slo_breach.csv, trace_snapshot_20280511.txt, and a short mitigation playbook.

— Rafael

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-13T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout slow tails & elevated error-rate — FastGate escalation and mitigation

Rafael / team — thanks for the fast triage and the clear remediation steps. Executive guidance and decisions: 

1) Approve keeping the concurrency bump to 40 for us-west-2 for a stabilizing window of 8 hours. Track cost delta hourly and prepare rollback criteria (backpressure reappearance OR cost > 2x baseline for the window).
2) Approve the proposed 10% usage credit to FastGate for the documented incident window; coordinate with Billing to log a one-time account credit under deal FG-2027-Q4-Expand.
3) SRE action: perform the GPU host health sweep now (Marcus to confirm completion) and schedule an ops post-mortem between Redwood ENG and FastGate for Friday at 10:00 PDT. Invite list: Rafael, Marcus, Marissa, FastGate ops (Samir), and an exec brief to Growth.
4) Tactical ask to Product: add a per-account context-length radar in Redwood Console so we can detect rising average token windows earlier. UX / Product to triage for Q3 roadmap.

Please prepare a short one-page executive readout (2 slides) summarizing root cause, customer impact, and the mitigation timeline. Rafael — please share updated SLO numbers and the CSV of affected requests with CS to close the loop.

— Hannah
VP, Customer Reliability & Escalations
Redwood Inference
